summary: Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (~1950–1956). He held positions at Psychiatrická nemocnice Kosmonosy, the National Institute of Public Health, Psychiatrické centrum Praha, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and California Institute of Integral Studies.
Indologist Stanislav Mudra earned his Ph.D. from Charles University's Faculty of Arts (~1929–1934), studying under doctoral supervisor Otakar Pertold.

Indologist and linguist Stanislav Šmelhaus studied at the First Faculty of Medicine and completed his Ph.D. at Charles University's Faculty of Arts (~1906–1925) under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý.

Indologist Stanisław Franciszek Michalski studied at the University of Warsaw, University of Vienna (Ph.D. under Leopold von Schroeder and Paul Kretschmer), and University of Göttingen (under Hermann Oldenberg and Jacob Wackernagel). He was a Docent at the University of Łódź (1945–1960).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Stanisław Schayer studied across Warsaw, Heidelberg, Freiburg (Ph.D.), Munich, and Lviv (Habilitation under Andrzej Gawroński). He served as an assistant professor (1929) and ordinarius Professor (1938) at the University of Warsaw.
Stanley Abe, a specialist in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, held an appointment at Duke University (attested 1995 and 2004).
Indologist and historian Stanley Cecil Sutton served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia University, Tübingen under Karl Hoffmann, and Yale (Ph.D. under Paul Thieme), where he was Edward E. Salisbury Professor from ~1976 to 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell (Ph.D.), and Harvard, and held posts at Ceylon, the University of Cambridge, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University (1976–2001).

Linguist and philosopher Stanley Lombardo studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin before holding a faculty post at the University of Kansas (~1976–2014).

Stanley Weinstein, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, studied at Komazawa, the University of Tokyo, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He held posts at Komazawa University, SOAS University of London, and Yale University.

Indologist and historian Stanley Wolpert earned his B.A. from City College of New York and M.A. from the University of Pennsylvania. He held assistant professor, associate professor, and department chair appointments at the University of California, Los Angeles starting in 1959.
Stefan Anacker, who worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1970) under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, having completed his dissertation at the University of Washington. He has held positions at Washington, Copenhagen, the University of Munich, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences.

Indologist and philosopher Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak studied under Leopold von Schroeder, Richard Simon, Adolf Kaegi, Antoine Meillet, Louis Finot, Sylvain Lévi, Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, and Andrzej Gawroński. He served as Professor at the University of Lviv (1928–1941).

Stefan Larsson, a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie, Erik af Edholm, and David Germano. He held research and teaching posts at Stockholm, UC Berkeley, KTH, and Gävle.

Stefan Mario Maul, a historian, archaeologist, and linguist, earned his doctorate at Göttingen and habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin. He held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, Heidelberg University as Ordinarius for Assyriology (1995), and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

Linguist and Indologist Stefan Mladenov studied at Sofia University, Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer), Saint Petersburg (under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay), and Charles University (Ph.D.). He held posts at Sofia University, becoming ordinary professor in 1921.

Stefania Travagnin, working in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, held posts at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) as assistant professor and centre director, and at SOAS University of London (~2020).

Stefano Zacchetti, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, earned his BA and PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice. He held positions at Venice, Soka University, and the University of Oxford as Yehan Numata Professor (2012–2020).
